approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from the best molecules scored in the current task. It draws parents from score quantiles, then uses fragment crossover with optional finishing mutation or short chains of atom and bond edits. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity checks and a sulfur gate reject duplicate graphs and new outside-envelope sulfur signatures beyond the largest count in an original scored generating parent. For each announced batch member it generates sixteen fresh admitted candidates. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted archive uses chiral Morgan occurrence counts, count-Tanimoto covariance and adaptive score normalization. Independent joint posterior function draws across that complete field choose distinct masked maxima. Real feedback updates the archive and a capped population of the best scored molecules.
approach.novelty: Reduce only the fresh field from sixteen to four candidates per announced batch member: forty competitors for the existing batch of ten. The inherited predictor and correlated Thompson choice law still rank the entire field. The recently measured wider-field sibling spent four times the generation work without enriching its selections; earlier siblings changed predictive laws, removed allocation components or removed mutation continuation. This is the previously untested downward contrast. Fewer competitors may reduce the advantage of extreme positive residual draws while retaining useful selections, which could improve actual incumbent progress at lower generation cost. Forty candidates may instead omit productive alternatives; neither sufficiency nor an optimal width is assumed.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is weak productive selection despite a costly fresh field, not a demonstrated shortage of candidates. Actual n-1744a1494180 summary.json/run.log pairs for all three issued Search seeds are complete: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. Per-task means are deco_hop 0.7069397917343436, drd2_docking 0.9910169833369453, median_2 0.22273152064211169, sitagliptin_mpo 0.6047677442780907 and zaleplon_mpo 0.4568095314519592. Its 435 complete 160-member fields contained 69,600 fresh admitted graphs from 76,081 breeding attempts, 6,349 duplicates, two invalid products and 130 sulfur rejections. Only 648 of 4,350 accepted offspring strictly beat their best original generating parent, and only 255 advance the sequential incumbent. Measured sibling n-da0eeecfb462 changes just pool_multiplier 16 to 64: all 435 fields reach 640 and 73.3 percent of selections reach beyond the original-sized prefix, yet selected mean enrichment falls from +1.054 to +1.043 pool SDs while the pool maximum rises from +1.735 to +1.841. Selected posterior SD relative to pool average rises from 0.849 to 0.897 and mean-argmax disagreement from 0.865 to 0.928. Mean actual offspring score falls from 0.3720 to 0.3601 despite slightly more local wins. Non-oracle task time rises from about 26.2 to 105.9 seconds; the complete endpoint delta is -0.016060430485631327, with seed deltas -0.044984249614889005, -0.012370936000374977 and +0.00917389415837, six cell gains and nine losses. This measured cost/quality split and open handoff h-065213eaad9d442d motivate the fixed downward contrast, not a claim that the residual signature caused the loss. The source control n-605c7a785b51 removed successful predictive allocation at full field effort and measured -0.12818290031998167 with fourteen losses and one gain; this supports retaining predictive allocation as historical source evidence, but its frozen catalog contribution interpretation is stale/needs_review, not newly assessed prerequisite support. The Parent's deco_hop seed-0 trajectory jumps from 0.609560453893309 at evaluation 280 to 0.8561477222467935 at 281. That inherited realization makes endpoint contrasts sensitive and remains in the registered fifteen-cell mean. All read Parent and source summary/run artifacts exist; their CPU-allocation warnings coexist with successful final receipts and are retained rather than suppressed.

literature_review.conclusion: The actual indexed n-da0eeecfb462 research_intent has literature_review=null, so there is no recorded node review to reuse. These are fresh actual searches, followed by reading two primary papers and official tutorial/implementation material. The searches find useful support for the finite-candidate posterior-maximization boundary and its compute scaling, but no useful primary evidence that reducing this molecular field from sixteen to four candidates per batch member will improve final Top-1 or preserve a sufficient search density. Approximation-focused search results do not answer this fixed-width question. The residual-extreme explanation is explicitly an inference from the Parent and newly measured wider sibling, tested through selected standardized residual leverage, real absolute productivity and complete endpoints. Register only the admitted one-line downward contrast; do not transfer an external sampler, sparse posterior or new dependency, redefine success as compute saving, or claim an optimum. End the exposed recipe if the complete +0.002 target fails.

sources.applicability: Supports preserving the Parent's joint-draw maximization and separating non-oracle cost from fixed-budget final Top-1. The continuous GP setting, parallel feedback and assumed model do not establish forty-candidate sufficiency for adaptively generated, gated molecular graphs. The query's ICML wording was corrected by the primary source's AISTATS publication.
sources.finding: Section 3 defines Thompson choice by maximizing a posterior function sample and extends it to synchronous batches through multiple draws. The paper distinguishes regret by evaluation count from regret by time; sample maximization is a computational challenge. Its guarantees are stated under a GP generative model, not a rule that enlarging or narrowing an arbitrary finite candidate field improves realized scores.
sources.title: Kandasamy et al. (AISTATS 2018), Parallelised Bayesian Optimisation via Thompson Sampling

sources.applicability: The finite-location exact-sampling cost applies to the Parent's dense pool covariance factorization. Its heteroscedastic risk objective, variational model and alternative sampler are not transferred; it gives no molecular endpoint guarantee or evidence that multiplier four is optimal.
sources.finding: Section 3.1 describes batch Thompson sampling as posterior draws followed by maximizers and notes that exact GP draws at finite input locations have cubic cost in their number. It develops a different sparse/decoupled sampling route for its quantile/expectile problem rather than recommending a particular finite field cardinality.
sources.title: Picheny et al. (UAI 2022), Bayesian Quantile and Expectile Optimisation

sources.applicability: Corroborates the expected reduction in pool-generation and covariance work from a smaller field while retaining exact conditional sampling. Asymptotic factorization reductions do not predict whole-task quarter time, since training, logging and oracle costs remain. Its continuous benchmark does not justify forty molecules or a score gain; no BoTorch code or dependency is imported.
sources.finding: The tutorial makes candidate count an explicit input to discrete Thompson sampling. Dense Cholesky sampling over m candidates costs O(m^3) work and O(m^2) covariance storage. It contrasts exact and approximate samplers and treats candidate generation and output batch cardinality separately.
sources.title: Official BoTorch v0.14.0 tutorial: Bayesian optimization with large-scale Thompson sampling

sources.applicability: Provides an official implementation reference for varying a finite choice field while keeping the predictive model. Its without-replacement deduplication differs from this Parent's sequential masks, so it is not substituted or assumed equivalent. Retain the exact inherited law and verify it on actual smaller fields; the code provides no width-four performance guarantee.
sources.finding: forward accepts an N-point candidate tensor and an independently specified num_samples, draws the joint model posterior at those points, and returns candidate indices by maximizing sampled objective values. The source makes finite-set membership an input to the sampler rather than a change to the predictive posterior's fitting rule.
sources.title: Official BoTorch implementation: botorch.generation.sampling.MaxPosteriorSampling

hypothesis: Reduce only CONFIG['posterior_selector']['pool_multiplier'] from 16 to 4, so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson selector chooses the announced batch through its original sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a complete fresh field of four admitted candidates per announced batch member (40 instead of 160 at batch ten), with every generator, admission, prediction, residual, survival and fallback law inherited.

finding_summary.headline: Forty-member fields cut work and residual extremes, but lower the complete endpoint mean
finding_summary.insights: Lower residual competition is real here, but it does not establish productive selection. The retained predictor gives exactly the same predictions as its passive original-model reference on the same real inputs; the lower selected-stream MSE on the Child is accompanied by worse pair ordering and batch rank correlation on a different accepted history. Generic core novelty rises, yet total incumbent progress and typed-core productivity fall. Future rank-band support is similar in aggregate, while fewer generation opportunities leave 355 eligible accepted records undrawn versus 50; this is measured exposure, not proof that reduced reuse caused the loss. The molecular assessment also finds useful compact aromatic amides and cyclic amines alongside reactive attachments, dense ring growth and unresolved stereochemistry. More ring-rich or novel structures do not guarantee preservation of favorable functional-group context, and the sulfur rule supplies no whole-molecule plausibility certificate. The complete loss and the still-negative sensitivity rule out a performance rescue by this fixed smaller-field recipe. They do not identify statistical or chemical mediation, an optimal width, a monotone width response, or a transferable benefit. The exposed recipe ends; whole-selector and whole-foundation contribution questions remain separate.
finding_summary.results: All 435 smaller fields filled and the original correlated sampler operated correctly. Breeding attempts fell from 76,081 to 18,643, and mean task non-oracle time fell from 26.20 to 16.72 seconds. Selected standardized residual leverage fell from 1.998 to 1.506 in every matched task/seed cell, supporting the predicted reduction in extreme positive residual competition. Selected mean enrichment nevertheless fell from 1.054 to 0.885 pool standard deviations. There were 650 strict generating-parent wins versus 648, but actual offspring scores averaged 0.3469 versus 0.3720, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819 to 4.883, with 220 advances versus 255. The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.534036, a paired change of -0.062417: thirteen of fifteen cells and all three seed means were lower. The +0.002 target fails despite lower seed dispersion. The Parent's rare late decoration-hopping breakthrough remains in the primary panel and contributes -0.015340 to the mean difference; the descriptive remaining fourteen-cell mean is still -0.050440. Total wall time rose because one decoration-hopping oracle run took much longer, so the demonstrated saving concerns non-oracle work.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and cyclic amines coexist with reactive attachments, dense ring growth and unresolved stereochemical identity
molecular.overall_character: Node n-fe16bf000919 produces recognizable fused aromatic amides, nitrogen-rich carbonyl systems, aryl/cyclic amines, azaaryl-linked dicarbonyl rings and fluorinated imino/dione frameworks. Different seeds produce different connectivities, while leading series within a seed often retain a scaffold and alter short chains, halogens or ring closures. This is moderate overall structural diversity with locally narrow leaders, rather than global scaffold collapse. All five Child digest tasks have 900 trajectory records including 870 accepted optimizer observations; all 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent paths were present and read. No task, path or seed comparison is missing. The immutable context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile mismatch. These accepted Search streams do not describe rejected or unselected generated pools. In the fixed task order, Child median heavy-atom counts are 25, 39, 29, 29 and 26, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27; corresponding Child median RDKit-perceived ring counts are 3, 7, 5, 5 and 4. Digest ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9667 to 0.9966 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9011 to 0.9897. These are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Charge-marker and stereocentre-marker incidence is 0.0 throughout; this does not mean basic amines or potentially stereogenic centres are absent. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing had no descriptor failures. It finds 2348 Child optimizer observations with unassigned tetrahedral centres versus Parent 2455, and no assigned tetrahedral observations in either accepted stream. Recognizable amide and cyclic-amine examples coexist with direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, acyl fluoride, peroxide, unusual N-S connectivity, small-ring cumulenes and exceptionally large fused structures. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable and medicinal chemistry quality weak overall, with substantial variation between molecules. Higher labels do not validate stability, geometry, synthesis or pharmacology. The structural audit and path hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r30-slot3-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. Every quoted complete SMILES is from the Child digest or a trusted Child Search trajectory. Parent chemistry uses its published trajectories and indexed full molecular assessment. Historical transferable gaps originate in Development node n-c55c3d520a2c, were carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and are re-observed here under the current profile, batch ten and 300 observations per objective. This preserves qualitative provenance and conditions; it pools no score effects and attributes no chemistry to a component.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact fused aromatic carboxamides with aryl or pyridyl partners. Seed 0 has a 24-heavy-atom indole-like amide, an N-F bond and an additional O-containing four-membered closure. Seed 1 has a 24-heavy-atom benzothiophene-like aryl amide with ethoxy and imino substitution, without a direct N/O-halogen bond. Seed 2 has a 25-heavy-atom indole/pyridyl amide carrying an O-linked ethynyl group and N-bromomethyl substitution. These are three or four perceived rings with substantial aromatic content. The accepted stream has median 25 heavy atoms, 240 sulfur-containing observations and 252 observations with direct N-halogen bonds. Recognizable amide connectivity is present, but the leading seed-0 and seed-2 attachments are chemically unusual.
liabilities: The leading N-fluoro amide and halomethyl/ethynyl ether substitution require local stability and synthesis assessment; ordinary carbon-bound fluorine is a distinct environment.
The seed-0 O-containing four-membered closure and a lower-label cyclic-cumulene aryl region raise separate geometric questions. Their graph validity does not establish accessible conformations.
missing_features: Conventional stable peripheral substitution is not consistently recovered with the favorable compact aromatic-amide arrangement: the strongest seed-0 example has N-F and the seed-2 example has N-CH2Br and an O-linked ethynyl group. The seed-1 leader is a counterexample to universal reliance on those bonds.

Chemically independent, readily plausible realizations of the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement remain limited among the leading series. The trajectories do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed endpoints are 0.45766047024715, 0.4463521672202675 and 0.45348083502552267, compared with Parent 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Methane, the acyclic divinyl ether and interhalogen fragments have zero labels; the late smaller azaaryl lactam scores 2.465623289227245e-10. A late cyclic-cumulene aryl amide scores 0.21440263746837318, below the seed-1 noncumulated benzothiophene amide. The visible association is compact complete aromatic/carbonyl organization, not ring or sulfur presence alone. The Parent includes a higher-label halogen-free azaindole/N-hydroxy amide; the Child still reaches a strong non-N/O-halogen family in seed 1. These examples do not establish that reactive halogen attachments are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: This stream combines aromatic heterocycles through carbonyl, amidine and heteroatom linkages, but its size and topology differ sharply by seed. Seed 0's 40-heavy-atom leader combines a substituted dione region, azaaryl groups, a thioester and an N-linked acyl fluoride. Seed 1's 27-heavy-atom amidine leader has densely cross-connected aromatic regions and several perceived four-membered closures, including O-containing closures. A methyl-imino analogue retains that framework without chloromethyl substitution. Seed 2 reaches a 73-heavy-atom fused nitrogen/carbonyl system with 13 perceived rings, N-N/N-O links, lactone-like regions and O-Br groups. Across the accepted stream the heavy-atom median is 39 versus Parent 31, with a maximum of 119 and median perceived ring count 7 versus Parent 4. This is ring-rich growth, much of it difficult to regard as ordinary synthetic chemistry.
liabilities: Acyl fluoride, direct O-Br bonds and N-O/N-N linkages need environment-specific assessment. O-halogen observations number 216 versus Parent 44; this is separate from a sulfur-envelope condition.

The amidine family's several four-membered closures and the large seed-2 polycyclic structures raise geometry, stability and synthetic-route questions. RDKit-perceived rings do not constitute a synthesis feasibility test.
missing_features: The Child does not recover the Parent's high-label compact linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione arrangement among its leaders; it instead supplies a dione/thioester, an amidine series or a much larger fused family. No general need for additional rings follows from that absence.

Plausible geometry and conventional peripheral chemistry are not established for the most densely connected Child families. A methyl-imino relative already avoids the chloromethyl group at the same label, but retains the difficult ring topology.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623 and tiny hydrocarbons or halogen fragments sit at 0.5. Child endpoints are 0.6260504201680672, 0.6313771954279342 and 0.5886452141832343 versus Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. The chloromethyl-imino and methyl-imino amidine relatives both score 0.6313771954279342; this does not support dependence on the chloromethyl attachment. The large seed-2 leader remains below the smaller seed-1 leader and well below the Parent seed-0 compact fused carbonyl/thione family reached at evaluation 281. More aromatic mass and ring closures do not recover that particular arrangement. This is a chemical comparison between actual histories, not evidence that a particular bond or field width caused their difference.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-label molecules carry aryl regions together with available aliphatic amine centres. Seed 0's 28-heavy-atom leader has an N-methyl pyrrolidine, a halogenated biaryl region, an azetidine-containing fused arrangement and an aminomethyl group. Seed 1's 26-heavy-atom leader has connected saturated nitrogen rings, aryl fluorine and an O-containing fused region. Neither of those leaders has direct N/O-halogen bonds. Seed 2 instead reaches a 31-heavy-atom chlorinated aryl/amine framework with an open allene segment and a small N-containing ring. Median size is 29 heavy atoms in both Child and Parent. These recognizable cyclic-amine families are more conventional locally than many other streams, although their connected topology and stereochemistry remain unverified.
liabilities: Dense connected saturated/small-ring topology can be challenging to synthesize. Small nitrogen rings themselves are recognizable chemistry; the concern is the complete geometry and connectivity, not their mere presence.

The seed-2 open allene is distinct from the more geometrically concerning cyclic cumulenes. Cyclic-cumulene observations number 15 versus Parent 1, and 853 of 870 Child observations have unassigned tetrahedral centres.
missing_features: Available cyclic and aliphatic amine centres are already present; there is no supported shortage of basic-nitrogen capability. The missing capability is consistent chemically credible topology and functional-group placement, especially in the altered seed-2 family.

Stereochemical identity is not specified: the seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders have respectively three, one and two RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres. The trajectories do not measure a penalty for this omission.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00017210440419041065, and its larger carboxylic-acid/amide relatives remain low. The nitrogen on the sulfonamide is chemically distinct from the available aliphatic amines in the leaders. Child endpoints are 0.990783775348799, 0.9878959770055941 and 0.922851891009479, compared with Parent 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. The visible association is the complete presentation of amine centres with aromatic regions, not total nitrogen, sulfur removal or size alone. The high labels establish neither measured protonation nor affinity, selectivity or synthetic access.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders link aryl or quinoline-like regions to nitrogen-rich carbonyl rings, often with alkyl and ether substitution. Seed 0's 28-heavy-atom leader is an aryl-S-N-linked cross-connected dicarbonyl system with ethoxy substitution. Seed 1 has a 31-heavy-atom propylamino quinoline connected to a fused dicarbonyl nitrogen ring. Seed 2 has a 32-heavy-atom alkylquinoline substituent attached through a chlorinated carbon to connected nitrogen rings containing carbonyl and amine functionality, with two perceived eight-membered cycles. Median heavy-atom count is 29 versus Parent 31; the Child median perceived ring count is 5 versus Parent 4. Nitrogen, carbonyl and aromatic groups are abundant rather than missing. Carbonyl-rich medicinal motifs coexist with demanding N-S, aminal-like and fused/medium-ring arrangements.
liabilities: The seed-0 aryl-S-N connection needs assessment in its complete electronic environment; permitted divalent sulfur does not certify the linked heterocycle's stability.
Fused nitrogen rings, medium-ring unsaturation and the seed-2 chlorinated amine-adjacent carbon create synthetic and geometric questions. None was tested by a synthesis or conformer measurement.
missing_features: Simpler feasible alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/amine/carbonyl relationship are not consistently established among leaders. This is not a demonstrated shortage of rings, nitrogen or carbonyl groups.
Stereochemical and conformational identity remain unresolved for the connected carbonyl-ring families; the three seed leaders have respectively one, one and two unassigned tetrahedral centres.

Methane scores 0.0, ethanol 0.014932027335788824, and the isolated amino/amide-ring fragment 0.07208691319279743. Child endpoints are 0.20422955404103896, 0.21304786601954073 and 0.2149896558044248, versus Parent 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. per_task.generated_character: The main family retains fused nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl or dione systems with fluorinated substituents and unsaturated carbocyclic regions. Seed 0's 25-heavy-atom leader has N-acetyl, N-methyl and N-fluoromethyl substitution, an imino group and a bridged sulfur-containing cycloalkene; it lacks direct N/O-halogen bonds. Seed 1's 26-heavy-atom leader is a cross-connected dione/phenol/ether framework with a difluoroalkyl group, also without direct N/O-halogen bonds. liabilities: Direct N-halogen observations fall from Parent 425 to Child 182, yet cyclic-cumulene observations rise from 1 to 50 and O-O observations from 16 to 40. Those are distinct chemical liabilities, not one general improvement or deterioration metric.

The seed-0 bridged sulfur cycloalkene and the seed-2 fluorinated cyclobutene have unassigned centres. Cyclic cumulenes and very large concatenations persist at both low and intermediate labels; useful sulfur and ordinary carbon-bound fluorine should remain distinguished from those geometries.

Geometrically credible, stereochemically specified alternatives are not consistently established across the leading families. The seed-0 and seed-1 examples avoid N/O-halogen bonds, so conventional nitrogen substitution is already possible; no exact missing target pharmacophore can be inferred.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; re-observed in n-fe16bf000919 on complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 with batch ten and 300 observations per objective. Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 525 of 4350 Child accepted optimizer observations versus Parent 786, while O-halogen bonds occur in 250 versus Parent 217. Leading output includes an N-fluoro amide, an acyl fluoride and O-brominated polycycles. A chloromethyl-imino/methyl-imino pair has the same observed label, and several cyclic-amine or carbonyl leaders have no N/O-halogen bond. The earlier narrow neutral sulfur-envelope condition is retained as context, not a whole-molecule plausibility certificate; its source score effect is not transferred here.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when modifying otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer environment-aware local transformations and conventional alternatives that preserve useful functional-group relationships learned from current observations. Distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens, useful amines and sulfur groups from reactive heteroatom attachments. These associations do not establish that a universal filter improves labels or attribute the motifs to one component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; re-observed in n-fe16bf000919 on complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 with batch ten and 300 observations per objective. Read-only structural parsing finds 67 Child accepted observations with a cyclic cumulated-carbon centre versus Parent 6. One sulfur/carbonyl relative with a small cyclic cumulene retains an intermediate label. Other leaders have dense four-membered closures, bridged sulfur rings or connected medium nitrogen rings. Compact aromatic amides and recognizable saturated cyclic amines are counterexamples to uniform geometric implausibility; ring richness is already present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring graphs from geometrically credible unsaturation and connected topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring transformations sensitive to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, and provide feasible alternate topologies retaining learned chemical relationships. Aromatic notation and sanitization cannot supply conformational evidence. The observed structures justify examining geometry, not a blanket ban on small, fused or medium rings, and establish no causal score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; re-observed in n-fe16bf000919 on complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 with batch ten and 300 observations per objective. Every Child digest stereocentre-string incidence is zero. RDKit perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2348 of 4350 accepted Child optimizer observations versus Parent 2455, with no assigned tetrahedral observations. A compact cyclic-amine leader has three unassigned centres, while some aromatic-amide and cross-connected dione leaders have none. The issue is conditional on a stereogenic structure, not every molecule; neutral strings coexist with clear aliphatic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic molecular arrangements remain incompletely specified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when meaningful, accounting for symmetry and configurational instability. Handle protonation and tautomerism separately from stereochemistry. These records establish missing specification, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific origin.

The evidence neither identifies a responsible operator nor guarantees endpoint gain.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer feasible scaffold transformations that retain favorable functional relationships learned from task-local feedback while changing connectivity beyond peripheral decoration. Assess their actual labels and chemical credibility separately; new strings and ring counts alone do not demonstrate useful coverage. This establishes no component attribution or general benefit from increasing diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
